messages:
maria: Quick sync — I'm proposing we standardize 429s across endpoints before the Dedicated rollout. Current behavior varies a lot across routes and it breaks SDK backoff logic.

Derek: +1. Can you outline the key incompatibilities you've seen?

maria: Sure — high level: 1) header names differ (some routes return Retry-After, others X-RateLimit-Reset or nothing), 2) body schemas differ (old endpoints return plain text while newer ones send JSON {error, code}), 3) burst semantics: some routes allow instant bursts without headers, others leak slowly.

sasha: Example from /v1/generate: we send `Retry-After: 3` (seconds) on some 429s, but also include `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` and `X-RateLimit-Reset: 1670000000` on others. SDK expects either Retry-After or an absolute reset timestamp, not both.

tj: That sucks for clients doing adaptive backoff. We should pick a single canonical set. Proposal: keep Retry-After (seconds) for simple clients, and provide optional X-RW-RateLimit-Reset (epoch seconds) for advanced use. Also normalize body to JSON with a stable `code` field.

maria: Exactly. Draft spec idea:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-RW-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RW-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RW-RateLimit-Reset: 1769511600
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "code": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "Per-minute quota exceeded for this route",
  "retry_after_seconds": 3
}
```

maria: Notes: keep Retry-After for compatibility, duplicate value as retry_after_seconds in the body for JSON consumers, and standardize on `X-RW-RateLimit-*` header prefix to avoid collisions.

anil: How will this interact with burst tokens? We have routes that allow short bursts via token-bucket with a separate burst pool. For those, Remaining may go negative or we just omit Remaining during bursts.

derek: Prefer not to return negative Remaining. Instead, include `X-RW-RateLimit-Burst-Window: 10` and `X-RW-RateLimit-Burst-Available: 2`. That tells clients how many extra requests they can make immediately. If burst pool exhausted, Remaining is 0 and Retry-After applies.

tj: Good idea. Also need to be explicit about clock skew: Reset should be epoch seconds in server time, but we must document that clients should prefer Retry-After seconds over absolute reset if clocks differ.

sasha: Backcompat concern: older SDKs expect Retry-After as integer seconds or a HTTP date. We're currently returning integer seconds in many places. If we switch to always include it, great. If we add RFC1123 date sometimes, it's okay if we document support but I'd rather keep it consistent as seconds.

maria: Agreement: always seconds for Retry-After. Also add a version header on 429s for schema evolution: `X-RW-RateLimit-Schema: 1`. Future changes increment it.

anil: Who owns the change? Runtime or API gateway? Rate limit evaluation happens in the edge gateway for many routes. We need a rollout plan so older gateways don't send mixed formats.

maria: Runtime + gateway co-owners: @sasha for gateway changes, @anil for runtime changes. We'll put a compatibility shim in gateway that maps existing internal flags to the new header names until all runtimes are updated.

derek: Tests: unit tests for header format, integration test that simulates bursts and checks headers/body, and SDK tests verifying backoff behavior given headers. Also add QA checklist for Dedicated customers since they run older versions.

tj: For SDKs: add helper that parses both Retry-After seconds and X-RW-RateLimit-Reset epoch. SDKs should prefer Retry-After seconds, fallback to reset - now we'll publish guidance.

sasha: One more edge case: automatic fallbacks when a route has per-customer quotas vs per-route quotas. We should include `X-RW-RateLimit-Scope: customer|route` so clients can decide to reroute or degrade features.

maria: Good call. Add it to the spec.

anil: Rollout plan idea: stage 1 (2 weeks) - gateway shim that emits new X-RW headers and normalized JSON body while retaining old headers; stage 2 (1 week) - runtime emits new headers natively and gateway can remove shim; stage 3 - SDKs pick up docs and helper helpers.

derek: Can we feature-flag the gateway shim per region so we can test EU customers first?

sasha: Yes, will add a per-region flag.

maria: Who can review the API contract doc? @derek @tj please. I'll draft a PR in the docs repo and ping infra afterwards.

tj: I'll review tomorrow. Also add a short postmortem-style test: simulate rapid burst, verify `X-RW-RateLimit-Burst-Available` decrements and then `Retry-After` appears.

derek: I'll add the integration test story. Also we should log the schema version in the audit logs for observability.

maria: Thanks all. Action items:
- maria: PR spec + examples (today)
- sasha: add gateway shim flag + mapping (this week)
- anil: implement runtime headers + burst fields (this sprint)
- derek: tests & SDK guidance (next week)
- tj: review spec + QA test cases (tomorrow)

infra-bot: Deploy window scheduled: Friday 02:00-05:00 UTC for gateway shim rollout in staging.

maria: Updated the PR link: https://git.redwood.dev/docs/rrate-limit-spec/compare. Ping me there for review. :thumbsup:
